newsitem.title: USA: United Ill. to build Conn. gas power plant.
newsitem.headline: United Ill. to build Conn. gas power plant.

text.p: The United Illuminating Co (UI) said Thursday it had an agreement in principle with Duke Energy Power and Siemens Power to build a 520 megawatt (MW) gas turbine power plant in Bridgeport, Conn.

"This $260 million project will provide Connecticut with additional generating capacity and the region with an important source of efficient, clean, low-cost energy that can eventually replace older, less-efficient sources," UI's chairman Richard Grossi said in a statement.
The new venture involving the three companies will be known as Bridgeport Energy, with phase one of the project expected to begin in September.
By next June, UI said two simple-cycle gas turbines will provide Connecticut with 340 MWs.
Phase two will be completed by 1999 when two heat recovery steam generators and a steam turbine will be added to increase the capacity of the project to 520 MWs.

The turbines, fired by natural gas, will incorporate advanced technology to operate at high efficiency with low nitrogen oxide emissions. Nitrogen oxide is a major contributor to the formation of ground-level ozone or smog pollution during summer.
UI said the project will also generate other benefits including:
- improve air quality in Fairfield County
- create up to 300 construction jobs over the next two years
- increase city and state tax revenues
- be compatible with Bridgeport's area economic development efforts.
Under the agreement, UI has an option to own up to one third of the new facility and purchase the power to help meet the electricity needs of its customers.
Duke Energy Power Services, a project investor, will supply the fuel and market the energy output.
Siemens Power Ventures is a co-investor.
UI is a New Haven-based electric utility that provides electricity and energy related services to more than 310,000 customers in 17 municipalities in the New Haven and Bridgeport, Connecticut, area.
Duke Energy Power Services, a unit of Duke Energy Corp, engages in electric power development in the U.S.
Siemens Power Corp is a U.S. affiliate of Siemens AG, a global leader in electrical engineering and electronics technology.
